summary: The draft mostly preserves explicit `[CONJ-DRAFT]` / `[RECALLED]` labeling, and the checked WTB/Khatri-Wilde citations are consistent with `docs/literature/WTB-2017.md` and `docs/literature/KhatriWilde-2020.md`; β.1 is basically bookkeeping, and β.2 correctly leaves the tele-simulation point open. The rejection point is structural: β.4 still assumes an unjustified Eve-simulation from channel environments to Charlie’s register, and β.5 reintroduces the core v0.3 mistake by treating Khatri-Wilde Prop. 19.2 as if it already reduced an adversarial comb to repeated uses of a fixed channel. Because that cross-space transfer is then used in the combined chain and the user-work plan, this is a retraction-pattern repeat, not just an incomplete draft.

issues.description: Lemma β.5 applies Khatri-Wilde Prop. 19.2 beyond what the cited source supports. `docs/literature/KhatriWilde-2020.md:36-42` states Prop. 19.2 for `n` uses of a fixed channel `N_{A→B}` inside an LOCC-assisted protocol. Lines 173-184 treat this as if it also settles the unresolved reduction from an adaptive adversarial Charlie comb to repeated uses of a single-shot effective channel `\tilde{\mathcal{M}}`, culminating in '因此 amortized bound inherits even for adversarial Charlie'. That is exactly the previously identified cross-task/cross-space gap, not a corollary of Prop. 19.2.
issues.suggestion: Keep β.G5 fully open until you either prove a comb-to-fixed-channel reduction or cite a theorem that directly handles adversarial combs/secret-key protocols. Remove the line-184 implication and the severity downgrade at line 193.

issues.description: Lemma β.4 assumes LOPC Eve can simulate Charlie’s register from `Env(E1) \cup Env(E2)`, but the key inference at lines 136-142 is not valid as stated. Measurement statistics of Charlie’s BSM on output systems `\hat A\hat B` are not generally determined by the reduced environment systems alone, and no degrading/simulation map from `(E_1,E_2)` to Charlie’s full classical/quantum side information is provided. This is more than 'technical non-triviality'; it is an unsupported premise for the claimed rate comparison.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite β.4 as an open comparison problem unless you can construct an explicit simulation/degrading map for the specific channel family. Do not claim LOPC Eve simulates umr Eve merely from possession of channel environments.

issues.description: The prose silently overstates closure even though the labels stay `[CONJ-DRAFT]`. The section title says 'Lemma β.4 ... (closes β.G4)', while lines 155-161 admit the lemma is not closable without further work, and lines 199-201 present the combined chain as if β.4 and β.5 were available. This is a silent upgrade in narrative form.
issues.suggestion: Rename β.4/β.5 section headers to 'attempted reduction' or 'draft route', and make §7 explicitly conditional on separate closure of β.G4 and the full β.G5 comb-to-channel step.

issues.description: The §9 Phase 1/2/3/4 plan misclassifies the hard work. WTB/Khatri-Wilde citation checking is realistic textbook verification, but β.G4 and especially β.G5 are not merely literature-verification tasks; they require new structural arguments. Putting SDP as the Phase-2 decision gate before those reductions are proved underestimates the novel work and blurs what C1+C2+C3 can actually certify.
issues.suggestion: Recast §9 so that β.G4 and β.G5 are primary theoretical blockers, separate 'PDF verification' from 'new proof required', and treat C1+C2+C3 as post-proof review rather than as a path that can itself close the structural gaps.

round_recommendation: Reopen β.G4 and β.G5 as the main blockers, remove the adversarial-comb to fixed-channel shortcut from Lemma β.5 and the derived chain in §7, then rerun review after the draft cleanly distinguishes verified literature facts from genuinely new reductions.
